PR: https://github.com/u2giants/theoracle/pull/282
Head SHA: `d44594eb0d5311961932ee62e60ac3a37e120c2a`
Reviewer: deepseek

## Findings

I have no further steps — the review is complete. Here is the consolidated report.

## Review: Eval feature (plan step 11), base `b16bbfe` → head `d44594e`

### Scope verified as correct
- Scoring math (`score_grade`: covered/total − 0.2·contradicted, floored at 0) and `normalize_grade` disjointness of covered/missing/contradicted are correct.
- Prompt rendering and hashing (`HASHED_PROMPTS`) are wired consistently.
- Admin authorization on run/upload/delete (`require_admin`) and the proxy's method/path forwarding are sound.
- Playwright seed data (`map_seed.py`) is internally consistent with `map.spec.ts` run diff/mean expectations.

### Findings

**F1 — Per-question failure isolation is incomplete (`apps/brain/brain/eval/run.py:267-271`).** The loop catches only `AnswerError`; `EmbedError` (a `RuntimeError`, `apps/brain/brain/embed.py:27`) raised from `embed_texts` inside the answer pipeline escapes. This contradicts the function's own docstring and `test_answer_failure_scores_zero_and_run_continues`. A single embedding failure aborts the whole run instead of scoring that question 0 and continuing.

**F2 — Eval page never refreshes after queuing a run (`apps/web/app/map/_components/eval-client.tsx:230-239`).** After `brainPost('/eval/run')` there is no polling/refetch; the UI stays on "Latest run: queued" until manual reload. The load effect at `:207-228` only runs on mount.

**F3 — Run diffs are keyed by question text, not id (`apps/brain/brain/api/eval.py:128-135`).** Diff compares `str(item.get("question"))`, while `question_id` is already recorded at `eval/run.py:253`. Duplicate question text (allowed by schema — no unique constraint) collapses or misattributes diffs.

**F4 — Queue deduplication is racy (`apps/brain/brain/api/eval.py:112-117`).** `INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` is check-then-insert without a lock/constraint; concurrent requests can enqueue duplicate `evaluate` jobs.

**F5 — Valid-but-empty grader response scores all-missing (`apps/brain/brain/eval/run.py:112-120`, `:160-170`).** `normalize_grade` accepts `{}` (or a response missing all keys) and treats every point as missing, rather than surfacing a grader failure. This silently low-scores on malformed model output.

**F6 — "Expected sources cited" can overstate (`apps/brain/brain/eval/run.py:272-278`).** `expected_sources_cited` derives from `answer["citations"]`, while `_finalize_local`/`_finalize_global` retain validated citations independent of the prose markers (`apps/brain/brain/answer/answer.py:303-328`, `:336-382`). Citation sets can therefore include sources the answer text never actually cited.

### Test gaps
- `apps/brain/tests/test_eval_fixture.py:74-84`: `EvalAnswers` synthesizes exactly one citation per distinct source, so F6 cannot be caught.
- `test_eval_fixture.py:104-117`: keyword-only `KeywordGrader` means malformed/empty grader output (F5) is never exercised.
- `apps/web/tests/map.spec.ts:130-149`: no browser coverage for admin add/delete question or the post-run refresh path (F2/F4).

### Verdict rationale
Core scoring and auth are correct, but F1 aborts runs on embed errors, F2 leaves the primary admin workflow stale, and F3–F6 are real correctness/quality defects with no covering tests. These warrant changes before merge.

## Question

How is Lodestar tested? For core: unit tests of the domain and use cases against in-memory fakes of the ports, or against SQLite? For datarepo: integration tests against a temporary SQLite database. For api: HTTP-level tests through axum (tower::ServiceExt) covering status codes, ETag/If-Match and the session cookie. For the frontend: Vitest unit tests, and whether the MVP has browser end-to-end tests (e.g. Playwright). What test data and fixtures are used?
title: Testing strategy

body:
Get the repo, docs and branding ready to make Hikidashi public.

### Where it stands

- The repo is **private**, has **no license**, no topics or homepage, and the
  description reads "…your saved instagram reels" (lower-case).
- `.github/` holds only `workflows/tests.yml`: no issue or PR templates, no
  `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` or `SUPPORT.md`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` is 18 lines describing our own workflow (branch per issue,
  changelog commit), not a guide for outside contributors.
- `README.md` is 435 lines and does the job of a manual. `CHANGELOG.md` is
  1,027 lines for v0.10.1.
- An icon exists (`app/web/icon.svg`, `frontend/static/icon.svg`); there's no
  wordmark, social preview image or demo media made for the public.

### 1. Privacy scrub (do this first; it decides how history is handled)

The repo contains data from a real library:

- **`docs/app.svg`** embeds real creators' @handles and thumbnails from the
  saved reels. These are other people's images, published from our repo.
  Regenerate it with `scripts/make_app_svg.py --placeholders` or a synthetic
  demo library.
- **`tests/search_eval.json`** lists real shortcodes from the library, which
  amounts to a partial list of what was saved. Move the real set out of the
  repo (e.g. into `data/`, git-ignored) and ship a synthetic example set with
  the same format.
- **Issue and PR threads** become public with the repo: screenshots (e.g. the
  card in spanthetree/hikidashi#27), measured examples and comments quoting real captions or
  handles. Review them, and edit or delete what's personal.
- **Git history** keeps all of the above even after the files change.
  Decide whether to:
  - rewrite history with `git filter-repo`
  - publish a fresh repo from a squashed snapshot
  - accept it

  Commit author emails are in history too; a `.mailmap` or a history rewrite
  can normalise them to the noreply address.
- `CLAUDE.md` is tracked: decide whether it stays public.

### 2. Licensing and legal

- **Choose a license** (MIT, Apache-2.0 or AGPL-3.0; AGPL if hosted forks
  should share changes). Add `LICENSE` and the SPDX field in `pyproject.toml`
  and `frontend/package.json`.
- **Third-party notices.** Models and tools have their own terms, and some
  restrict use:
  - embeddinggemma (Gemma terms of use)
  - jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual (CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial; verify)
  - faster-whisper / Whisper weights
  - Ollama models (qwen2.5)
  - yt-dlp, tesseract
  - map tiles and the Nominatim usage policy

  List them in `THIRD_PARTY.md` (or `NOTICE`), and say that weights are
  downloaded, not redistributed.
- **Trademark and affiliation.** Add a "not affiliated with or endorsed by
  Instagram or Meta" line to the README and the app's about/footer. Review
  the default "Instagram" theme (README: "Instagram by default"): use of the
  name, and how closely it copies their look and logo, if at all. Rename it
  to something descriptive if needed.
- **Terms of use.** An FAQ entry: it archives your own saves from your own
  export, downloads with yt-dlp for personal use, and the responsibility
  stays with the user. No circumvention claims.
- **Name check.** Done in spanthetree/hikidashi#121: "ReelVault" was taken (a commercial
  Instagram downloader and several GitHub repos), so the app is now
  Hikidashi.

### 3. Branding

- **Logo:** refine the icon so it works at 16 px (favicon) up to 512 px, plus
  a horizontal wordmark, light and dark variants, and the SVG source in
  `docs/brand/`.
- **Social preview** image (1280×640) for the GitHub repo card.
- **One-line tagline and short description,** used the same way in the
  README, the repo description, the image labels (#77), and the Unraid and
  TrueNAS templates (#87).
- **Demo library:** a synthetic set of reels (royalty-free or generated
  thumbnails and captions) used for every screenshot, GIF and the README hero
  image, and reusable as the Playwright seed (#39).
- **Screenshots and a short demo GIF or video:**
  - search by meaning
  - the detail sheet
  - recipes
  - map
  - themes
  - Japanese UI

### 4. Documentation

- **README as a landing page,** ideally under ~150 lines:
  - what it is and why
  - a hero image
  - key features
  - quick start (Docker, published image)
  - links into `docs/`

  Move the configuration table, hardware notes and deep detail into `docs/`.
- **Badges:** CI, latest release, license, GHCR image.
- **FAQ:** is this allowed, does it need my Instagram password (no), what
  leaves my machine, hardware requirements, GPU or not.
- **Docs site (optional):** MkDocs Material on GitHub Pages from `docs/`, with
  search. Decide if the Markdown on GitHub is enough.
- **`README.ja.md`,** since the UI ships in Japanese (#33).
- **Changelog:** keep it, but make releases readable. Summarise everything up
  to the first public version in one entry, and use GitHub Releases with
  notes from then on.
- **Proof-read the docs for internal shorthand:** issue numbers without
  context, references to "the desktop" or "the Unraid box" that assume our
  own setup.

### 5. Community and repo setup

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` rewritten for outsiders:
  - dev setup (link `docs/development.md`)
  - tests, lint and format (`ruff`, `mypy --strict`, vitest, Playwright)
  - branch and PR conventions
  - the changelog/version rule
  - how to add a translation
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant).
- `SECURITY.md`, with GitHub private vulnerability reporting turned on.
- Issue forms (bug report with version, install method and logs; feature
  request) and a PR template with the changelog checklist.
- Repo settings:
  - description, topics (`self-hosted`, `instagram`, `sqlite`, `svelte`,
    `fastapi`, `semantic-search`, `whisper`, `ollama`, `unraid`…), homepage
  - social preview
  - Discussions on or off
  - branch protection on `master`
  - Dependabot
- **First public release:** decide the version (`1.0.0`, or stay `0.x`), tag
  it, publish the images (#77), and write release notes.

### Done when

- [ ] No real library data, creator images or personal details in the files,
      the history (per the decision above), or public issue threads
- [ ] `LICENSE`, SPDX fields, `THIRD_PARTY.md` with model and data licenses
- [ ] Non-affiliation notice; Instagram theme reviewed
- [x] Name check done
- [ ] Logo, wordmark, favicon set, social preview committed under
      `docs/brand/`
- [ ] Synthetic demo library, used for all screenshots, the GIF and the
      README hero
- [ ] README as a landing page with badges, quick start and FAQ; detail moved
      to `docs/`
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY, issue forms, PR template
- [ ] Repo metadata and settings set; first public release tagged with images
      published
- [ ] Repo flipped to public

Related: spanthetree/hikidashi#77 (published images), spanthetree/hikidashi#87 (Unraid/TrueNAS install), spanthetree/hikidashi#88
(architecture docs), spanthetree/hikidashi#39 (Playwright seed data), spanthetree/hikidashi#33 (Japanese)
title: Polish documentation and branding for public release
